extDescription.message: Save HLS/DASH streams as one MKV/MP4 with the audio tracks and subtitles you pick. No re-encoding, nothing to install.

engineBrowserHelp.message: Nothing to install. Files go to the browser's Downloads folder. HLS only.

engineNativeHelp.message: DASH too, any destination folder, merging with ffmpeg.

speedLimitHelp.message: For all downloads together. In-browser engine: applies at once, also to running downloads; local app: to the downloads started after the change.

autoDetectHelp.message: When off, the extension doesn't watch network traffic until you press “Detect” on a tab.

clearHistoryTitle.message: Removes finished, failed and cancelled downloads from the list (the saved files stay)

openPage.message: Open the Fluxy page: downloads, settings, info

githubTitle.message: Fluxy on GitHub: code, releases, issues

aboutText.message: Fluxy saves the HLS/DASH streams and the videos of a page as one MKV/MP4, with the audio tracks and subtitles you pick, without re-encoding.

aboutIssues.message: Report a problem or suggest a feature

aboutLicense.message: Free software: GNU GPL v3.0 or later, with additional terms (attribution, name and logo).

aboutThird.message: Built with Mediabunny (MPL-2.0); the optional local app uses FFmpeg and yt-dlp.

aboutDonate.message: Fluxy is free. If it's useful to you, you can support it on Ko-fi:

errInterrupted.message: Interrupted when the browser was closed: retry to continue

otherVideos.message: Other videos ($p1$): previews, animated backgrounds, short clips

hintAdaptive.message: $p1$ video(s) on the page use an adaptive player: if the one you want isn't listed, press “Detect” and start it.

hintDrm.message: $p1$ video(s) on the page are DRM protected and can't be saved.

embedText.message: Player embedded from another site: the local app can analyse it with yt-dlp.

detectTitle.message: Reload the page and catch the streams the player loads

pillBrowserTitle.message: Download and merge in the browser, nothing to install

cryptoMissing.message: yt-dlp can't find pycryptodomex: encrypted (AES-128) streams will be downloaded by ffmpeg one segment at a time, much more slowly. To install it:

nativeChosenMissing.message: You chose the local app, but it isn't installed.

nativeCommError.message: Communication error with the local app:

installerSaved.message: Installer saved to Downloads. Open a terminal and run:

installerExplain.message: It copies the app to ~/.local/share/fluxy, registers it in Brave/Chrome/Firefox and offers to install ffmpeg and yt-dlp if they're missing.

noStreamsYet.message: No streams yet. Start playing the video: streams show up here as soon as the player loads them.

autoOff.message: Automatic detection is off. Press “Detect”: the page reloads and the streams the player loads show up here.

drmProtected.message: DRM protected ($p1$): it can't be downloaded.

liveStream.message: Live stream: only what's already available will be downloaded.

encryptionOk.message: $p1$ encryption with a clear key: supported.

skipTrack.message: Skip this track: stop it and leave it out of the file

aboutCws.message: Fluxy on the Chrome Web Store (Chrome, Edge, Brave…)

castEmpty.message: Nothing is being cast. In the popup, pick "Cast" on a stream, choose video, audio and subtitles, then the TV.

castSearchTitle.message: Search the network for Chromecasts and DLNA TVs

castNoDevices.message: No TV yet: search the network

castNoneFound.message: No TV found. Check that it is on and on the same network; if the PC has a firewall, see below or add the TV by address.

castAddHelp.message: Add a TV by address when the search can't see it: the IP of a Chromecast, or the description URL of a DLNA TV.

castStale.message: not seen in the last search

castRouteAutoHelp.message: Tries the TV on its own first (nothing to open on this PC), then the same TV under its other protocol, and only as a last resort through the local app.

castRecastTitle.message: Cast again now, from the current position

castTracksFixed.message: This TV is playing the original stream by itself: audio and subtitles are the ones it picks. To choose them, cast through the local app.

castAllow.message: Allow the TV to connect to this PC

castAllowHelp.message: To choose audio and subtitles the TV must take the video from this PC: the system will ask your password once to allow it from the home network.

castAllowWaiting.message: Waiting for the password in the system window…

castAllowDone.message: Allowed: casting again through the local app…

castFirewallClosed.message: The firewall of this PC ($p1$) blocks the TVs: casting works, but they choose audio and subtitles by themselves.

castFirewall.message: The local app finds TVs on UDP ports 5353 (Chromecast) and 1900 (DLNA), and with "through the local app" the TV fetches the video from this PC on TCP port 8790: if the PC has a firewall, allow them from the home network (with ufw: sudo ufw allow from 192.168.1.0/24 to any port 8790 proto tcp, and the same with port 1900 proto udp for DLNA TVs).

castRouteHelp.message: How the TV gets the video

castRouteRelayHelp.message: The local app fetches the stream with the page's headers and passes it on to the TV: works with protected streams.

castRouteDirectHelp.message: The TV fetches the original address by itself: lighter for the PC, but many sites refuse it (no cookies, no CORS).

castNeedsApp.message: Casting goes through the local app: install it to cast to Chromecasts and DLNA TVs.

castPickDevice.message: Choose a TV first (search the network)

castDirectHint.message: Try the "through the local app" route: the site may refuse requests that don't come from its page.

castVolumeFixed.message: The volume is set on the TV (fixed on this device)

castVideoAuto.message: Quality chosen by the TV (direct route): use the local app route to pick it

hint429.message: The site is limiting requests (too many at once). Wait a few minutes, lower concurrent downloads and connections in the settings, then retry.

loadWarn.message: Up to $p1$ connections at once. Some sites block your IP, even for days, when they get too many requests together: if a site starts refusing downloads, go back to 2 downloads and 8 connections.

sameSiteWarn.message: $p1$ downloads from $p2$ at the same time: some sites block the IP if they get too many requests. If errors start, pause one.

hint403.message: The server refused the request: the link may have expired. Retry renews it; if that's not enough, reopen the page, press Detect and retry.

pageCardText.message: YouTube doesn't use standard HLS/DASH playlists: the local app can analyse the page with yt-dlp.

errPickOne.message: Select at least one video, audio or subtitle track

srtTitle.message: Download only this subtitle track, as an .srt file

errNeedsHost.message: This stream needs the local app (ffmpeg + yt-dlp): install it from ⚙ → Engine.

errEngineRestarted.message: Interrupted: the in-browser engine was restarted

errSuspended.message: Interrupted: the browser suspended the extension

errWindowsInstaller.message: Automatic installation isn't available on Windows yet.

errMissingFile.message: File $p1$ missing from the extension: run ./build.py

hostTimeout.message: The local app didn't answer in time

offscreenJustification.message: Downloads the segments and merges the tracks into one file

eng_httpDenied.message: — the server refuses the request: reopen the page and press Detect to refresh the permissions

eng_notHls.message: The file doesn't look like an HLS playlist

eng_noTrack.message: No $p1$ track in the downloaded file ($p2$)

eng_noSpace.message: Not enough space: about $p1$ GB free needed, the browser allows $p2$ GB

eng_badRange.message: The server doesn't honour partial downloads: try again
